points.description: States that when two elements combine to form more than one compound, the masses of one element that combine with a fixed mass of the other element are compared (mass data from the compounds).
points.partial_credit: 1 to 2 marks if only some parts are stated, e.g. compounds or mass data mentioned but no fixed mass of one element.

points.description: States that the masses of the second element (per fixed mass of the first) are in a simple whole-number (integer) ratio.
Links the whole-number ratios to the conclusion that the element comes in discrete, indivisible units, because only whole numbers of units can combine (no fractions).
points.partial_credit: 1 mark if whole numbers are linked to 'units' or 'discrete' only vaguely, or the link is implied but not stated.

points.description: States that the smallest indivisible unit of mass of an element is the atom, so matter is made of atoms.
points.partial_credit: 1 mark if the atom is named but not tied to being the indivisible unit of mass.

rubric.notes: Full marks need the fixed-mass comparison of compounds, the whole-number ratio, the link from whole numbers to indivisible units, and the naming of that unit as the atom. The link in P3 must be stated as cause and effect; just saying 'whole numbers' and 'atoms' side by side earns no P3 marks. Restating the law or giving a general definition of atoms earns nothing by itself; a wrong statement loses only the marks of the point it sits in.
